standard.title: Develop skills for manipulating elements
standard.description: develop listening skills and skills for manipulating elements of music when singing and playing instruments
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have developed listening skills for specific purposes and basic singing/instrumental technique (AC9AMU2D01). They can match pitch with developing accuracy and demonstrate correct technique for classroom instruments. They have not yet focused on manipulating elements deliberately to create and control intended effects.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop listening skills and skills for manipulating elements of music to create controlled expressive effects when singing and playing instruments.

nodes.label: Manipulating elements during performance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can manipulate at least one element of music (e.g. dynamics, tempo, articulation) during singing or playing to create a specific intended effect.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate one deliberate element manipulation during singing or playing (e.g. gradually getting louder, or changing articulation from smooth to detached) and describe the effect.
nodes.typical_width: Manipulate elements across a range of singing and instrumental contexts — varying dynamics in repeated sections for interest, using articulation to suit different lyrics, choosing instruments for specific mood effects, using melodic steps and jumps to suit different sections of a piece.
wider: Perform the same section twice with different element manipulations — compare the effects and discuss which better suits the music's intention
Focus on a single element (e.g. articulation) across three different pieces — how does manipulating the same element produce different effects in different musical contexts?
nodes.hinge_reason: The ability to execute deliberate element manipulations during performance — not just plan them in composition — is a separate skill that requires practice. Students who can plan manipulations but not execute them under performance conditions cannot achieve the descriptor's requirements. This also underpins AC9AMU6D01 which requires developing expressive facility and control.

response_modes.reason: Element manipulation during performance requires the technique to be sufficiently automatic that it can be executed while simultaneously monitoring other aspects of performance. Repeated targeted practice — isolating one manipulation and drilling it across multiple repetitions before integrating — builds this automaticity.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one deliberate element manipulation during singing or playing
Can describe the intended effect of the manipulation

nodes.label: Listening to evaluate and compare effects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can listen to the effects they create by manipulating elements and evaluate which manipulations work better for the musical intention.
nodes.minimum_width: Listen to two versions of a short piece (or two attempts at the same section) with different element manipulations; describe one difference and say which they prefer and why.
nodes.typical_width: Listen to and evaluate effects of element manipulation across multiple dimensions — compare how easy/difficult different manipulations are to perform accurately, ask 'What works and why', listen to diverse music examples to identify how others have used elements and compare with their own choices.
wider: Listen to diverse music examples and identify how rhythm, pitch and timbre are used — use these observations to inform choices in their own compositions or performances
Record two rehearsal attempts with different manipulations, listen back and write a brief comparison — practise the language of musical evaluation

response_modes.reason: Evaluative listening is a skill that needs scaffolding — students default to 'I liked it' without structure. Build evaluation language: 'What changed between the two versions?', 'Which version better communicates the mood?', 'How difficult was version two to perform accurately?' These questions develop the feedback loops that drive musical improvement.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing diverse music examples from different contexts and cultures for how elements are manipulated gives students a much richer language for evaluating their own choices — each new example adds to their library of possibilities.
success_criteria: Can compare two versions of a musical passage and identify at least one difference in element manipulation
Can give a reason for preferring one version over the other in terms of the music's intended effect

nodes.label: Notation as a performance tool
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can read from staff, graphic and/or invented notation during rehearsal and performance, using it to guide element manipulation decisions.
nodes.minimum_width: Read from at least one notation type during rehearsal; follow at least one element-related instruction in the notation (e.g. a dynamic marking or a tempo change).
nodes.typical_width: Practise reading from staff, graphic and/or invented notation as an integral part of rehearsal and performance; invent a graphic score to represent specific sounds and use it in rehearsal; make adjustments to notation to ensure it is accurate and useful.
wider: Invent a graphic score to represent environmental or found sounds — refine it through rehearsal to ensure it accurately captures the intended manipulations
Compare reading from a graphic score vs a staff score for the same piece — discuss what information each type conveys and what each leaves out

response_modes.reason: Students at Y3-4 benefit from building a repertoire of notation types they can read fluently, not just one they have memorised. Graphic, staff and invented notation each have different uses and learning to switch between them prepares students for the range of documentation formats required in Y5-6 and beyond.

success_criteria: Can read from at least one notation type during rehearsal and follow its instructions
Can contribute to creating or refining a notation document to better capture intended manipulations
